title: ASME B31.3 Pipe Thickness Calculator
meta_description: Calculate minimum required pipe wall thickness per ASME B31.3 for process piping maintenance and inspection planning.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Required thickness t = P D / [2(S E + P Y)] + c per ASME B31.3 para. 304.1.2. Ferritic steels through 482 °C use Y = 0.4.

title: Pipe Schedule & Dimension
meta_description: Look up ASME B36.10M pipe outside diameter, inside diameter, wall thickness, and unit weight by NPS and schedule.

formula_json.formulaBasis: OD, ID, wall, and unit weight from ASME B36.10M by NPS and schedule.

title: Flange Dimension & Weight
meta_description: Look up ASME B16.5 weld neck RF flange dimensions, bolt circle, and approximate weight for Class 150, 300, and 600.

formula_json.formulaBasis: WN RF dimensions and mass from ASME B16.5. Hub bore follows ASME B36.10M pipe ID. RF stud length is a two-nut screening value.

title: Fitting & Valve Face-to-Face
meta_description: Look up ASME B16.10 flanged valve face-to-face dimensions by NPS and pressure class.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Valve face-to-face from ASME B16.10 flanged RF tables.

title: Butt-Weld Fitting Dimensions
meta_description: ASME B16.9 butt-weld fitting center-to-end and end-to-end dimensions with matching pipe schedule OD, ID, and wall.

formula_json.formulaBasis: 90° LR A = 1.5 × NPS(in) = 38.1 × NPS(mm basis). SR A = 1.0 × NPS(in). Bevel 37.5°.

title: Gasket Dimension & Selection
meta_description: Look up ASME B16.20 spiral wound and RTJ ring gasket dimensions by NPS and pressure class.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Spiral-wound and RTJ ring dimensions from ASME B16.20, matched to the B16.5 flange class.

title: Valve Cv Sizing Calculator
meta_description: Size control valves for liquid and gas service by calculating required flow coefficient (Cv) from process conditions.

formula_json.formulaBasis: US Cv per ISA / IEC 60534. Liquid Cv = Q_gpm √(SG / ΔP_psi) after converting m³/h and bar.

title: Bolt Torque & Tensioning
meta_description: Look up ASME PCC-1 recommended flange joint assembly torque, stud size, bolt count, and star tightening sequence.

formula_json.subtitle: ASME PCC-1 Guidelines for Pressure Boundary Bolted Flange Joint Assembly.
formula_json.formulaBasis: Assembly torque, stud size, and star-pattern tightening follow ASME PCC-1 for pressure-boundary bolted flange joints. NPS and class nominators come from the ASME B16.5 flange geometry used with the joint.

title: Blind Flange Thickness
meta_description: Calculate ASME B31.3 / VIII-1 UG-34 flat blind thickness t = d × √(0.3P / SE) + c from diameter, design pressure, and corrosion allowance.

formula_json.subtitle: t = d × √(0.3P / SE) + c using attachment factor C = 0.30 (B31.3 304.4.1 / VIII-1 UG-34).
formula_json.formulaBasis: Required thickness uses t = d × √(0.3P / SE) + c. C = 0.30 is the ASME Section VIII Division 1 UG-34 / B31.3 para. 304.4.1 bolted flat-cover factor. d is inside or gasket contact diameter; P and S share stress units; c is corrosion allowance.

title: Metal Weight & Cost Estimator
meta_description: Estimate metal weight and procurement cost for plate, pipe, and bar shapes using material density and unit price.

formula_json.formulaBasis: Mass = density × volume for plate, pipe, and bar. Densities are typical CS / 304 / Al / Cu screening values.

title: Hydro/Pneumatic Test Pressure
meta_description: Calculate ASME B31.3 hydrostatic and pneumatic test pressure with St/S temperature correction and yield-limit screening.

formula_json.subtitle: ASME B31.3 St/S stress ratio & yield limit check
formula_json.formulaBasis: Hydrostatic test pressure Pt = 1.5 × P × (St/S). Pneumatic Pt = 1.1 × P × (St/S) per ASME B31.3 para. 345.4.2. St is allowable stress at the test temperature and S is allowable at the design temperature. Default St/S = 1.0; field guide cap is 6.5. Confirm that test hoop stress stays below yield.

title: Thermal Expansion & Loop Sizing
meta_description: Calculate ASME B31.3 thermal growth and screen L-shape / U-loop leg length from material, T1/T2, and straight-run length.

formula_json.subtitle: ΔL = α L ΔT with guided-cantilever loop screening. Not a CAESAR II / Appendix P computer analysis.
formula_json.formulaBasis: Thermal expansion ΔL = α × L × (T2 − T1) using mean coefficients typical of ASME B31.3 Appendix C. L-shape min. guided length L = √(3 E D Δ / (4 Sa)). U-loop width taken as 0.65 L. Screening only.

faq.q: Does this replace a flexibility analysis?
faq.a: No. It is a field screening estimate for expansion loop size. Formal analysis is required where B31.3 flexibility rules are not obviously satisfied.

title: Pressure Drop & Friction Loss
meta_description: Darcy–Weisbach pressure drop with NPS/schedule ID, fittings as equivalent length, and ΔP in bar and psi.

formula_json.subtitle: ΔP = f (L/D) (ρ v² / 2) with Haaland friction factor for commercial steel pipe.
formula_json.formulaBasis: Darcy–Weisbach equation. Friction factor by the Haaland approximation to Colebrook. Elbow / gate / globe equivalent lengths use Crane TP-410 typical L/D values.

faq.q: Are steam and air densities fixed?
faq.a: Yes — typical screening densities. For HP steam or compressed air, treat the result as order-of-magnitude only.

title: Flow Rate & Velocity
meta_description: Compute pipe velocity v = Q/A and flag API RP 14E erosion velocity limit vc = c / √ρ.

formula_json.subtitle: Mean velocity versus API RP 14E erosion velocity. Safe / Warning / Erosion Risk.
formula_json.formulaBasis: v = Q / A using ASME B36.10M inside diameter. Erosion limit vc = c / √ρ with ρ in lb/ft³ per API RP 14E. Default c = 100 for continuous service.

faq.q: What c factor should I use?
faq.a: c = 100 is conservative continuous service. 125–150 is common for intermittent two-phase; site standards prevail.

title: Quick Engineering Unit Converter
meta_description: Convert plant units: pressure, dimension, temperature, flow, torque, weight, and velocity.

formula_json.subtitle: Seven categories: pressure, dimension, temperature, flow, torque, weight, and velocity. Also available from the floating Quick Unit dock.
formula_json.formulaBasis: Exact SI conversion factors. Torque uses 1 ft·lb = 1.355817948 N·m and 1 kgf·m = 9.80665 N·m. Mass uses the avoirdupois pound and metric tonne (1000 kg). Velocity uses 1 ft = 0.3048 m. Mass/volume flow uses the entered density (default 1000 kg/m³ water).

faq.a: The ⚡ Quick Unit button stays on the lower right of every public page except this full converter.
